items.excerpt: Wonder Dynamics co-founder Nikola Todorovic walks through Autodesk Flow Studio's new 3D Editor + Canvas, which pairs interactive 3D scene construction with generative 2D video models so AI shots can be blocked and re-staged rather than re-rolled from prompts.

EditShare is bringing GPU-powered Flow AI processing into its EFS storage nodes at IBC, expanding AI-assisted transcription and search to 13 languages so post teams can hunt footage across international content from inside the MAM.
Emmy-nominated VFX supervisor Aladino Debert breaks down the shot pipeline behind Noah Hawley's 'Alien: Earth,' including how synthetic-human effects and creature work were split across vendors.
DP Marshall Adams details the camera, lensing and color workflow he built with Vince Gilligan for Apple TV's 'Pluribus,' and how the look was locked from set through the DI.

A filmmaker who recovered a lost Billy Joel radio interview rebuilt the singer as an AI performer to carry the documentary — a test case for synthetic re-creation of a living artist who never consented.

The MPA and ByteDance struck an IP-protection agreement covering the Seedance video models, TikTok and other products, setting guardrails on what studio-owned characters and footage generative video tools will reproduce.
WildBrain is buying Personality AI, the company behind conversational 'Hey Peppa Pig' experiences, folding real-time GenAI character performance into a legacy kids IP catalogue.

Naoko Yamada, Abel Gongora and Kenichi Yoshida walk through how Science Saru translated Tomato Soup's manga artwork and pacing into animation for 'Jaadugar: A Witch In Mongolia' — a fully hand-authored process detailed shot by shot.

'The Iron Giant,' 'Ratatouille' and 'Spider-Verse' veteran Michel Gagne created, directed and animated the 60-minute feature 'The Saga of Rex' almost entirely by himself — a one-artist production model arriving as studios pitch automated pipelines.
Joseph Bell's third annual free VFX & Animation World Atlas charts 140,000+ artists at 2,900 companies, finds 2.7% net industry growth, and says the data shows no evidence AI has cut VFX jobs.

Abigail Hing Wen's hybrid animated/live-action short follows parents who turn a grieving child's drawings into an AI-powered virtual sanctuary — a film about generative AI made deliberately without it.
Six thousand entrants each cut a three-minute film about a future worth living in; ten finalists present live in downtown LA on Sept 25, with the winner taking a $2.5M grant to actually build it.
Important Looking Pirates' breakdown for 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' shows how Zeb and the film's environments were built, layer by layer, from plate to final composite.
DNEG's shot-by-shot breakdown for 'Star City' walks through the environment builds, digital doubles and destruction work behind the film's largest sequences.
Framestore VFX supervisors Stephane Naze and Benjamin Loch detail the flight, creature and environment work on 'Supergirl,' and how the team divided shots across facilities.
Oslo's Storm Studios explains the creeping vines, teleporting taxis and rock-like Sirens of 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians' season two, including the custom simulation setups behind them.
DNEG expanded Happy Valley for 'For All Mankind' season five, delivering the K-Station explosion, agricultural dome destruction and a full-CG spacecraft launch.
Base FX turned 'Beef' season two into a creature showcase — ants, bees, a coyote attack and CG aircraft — and walks through the sims and asset builds that made the invisible work land.
A closer look at how 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians' season two's rock-like Sirens were built with custom Bullet and Vellum solvers rather than off-the-shelf presets.
A making-of on the new 'Lord of the Flies' adaptation shot on Blackmagic's Pocket Cinema Camera 6K Pro, covering the small-camera rigging and grading choices that carried a feature look.
Believe.tv's 'OFF! Scratch' spot leans on tactile, hand-built motion design and character animation — a reminder of what a fully art-directed frame still buys you.
Apple's new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra is pitched squarely at on-device AI, and No Film School digs into which of those gains actually reach video editors and colorists.

Tencent's WorldClaw generates an entire editable 3D world from a text prompt rather than a flat video clip — a demo of prompt-to-set that lands closer to previs and virtual production than to text-to-video.
Corridor Crew's artists try to hit a 1990s VFX pipeline with 1990s constraints, exposing how much of today's speed is tooling rather than craft.
